summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge by analysing Soony's confidential supply-chain data, finding hidden launch risks, and building a general recheck-and-act agent product (Lighthouse) with a polished UI, ready for a 12:45 hand-in on Sunday.
summary.outcome: Data analysis surfaced the real Collector's Edition shortfalls (overbooked art books, failed statue lot, sleeve revision conflict, false magnet alarm) and later drops; a versioned poller plus LLM agent and a web UI were built. UI polish included a 'How we got here' case flow, routine step-menu fixes, top bar and phone layout fixes. Many commits on `main` remain unpushed (about 19+ ahead of origin) as the hand-in approaches.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in gitignored `data/` (raw, drops, notes, img); `.env` is gitignored and `.env.example` is committed. Never put data values in code.

The Soony portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip; no webhooks or notifications. Files are replaced under the same name without notice, so polling must compare SHA-256 checksums, not just filenames.
Team workflow files `CLAUDE.md` and `PROGRESS.md` exist; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
The API server does not load `.env` on import, so new settings such as `ASK_VIEWER_TITLE` need a helper that loads `.env` first or they are missing after restart.

Routine steps are validated per watched kind: 'Chase once if no answer' only works on routines watching messages awaiting an answer, and 'Ask for a status' only on shipment watchers; the server rejects others with 'step N cannot be done on open decisions'.
The routine diagram's connector and node components are exported from `FlowGraph.tsx` and reused by `CaseFlow.tsx`, so both visuals share the same code.
Routines calls Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`) using the key from `.env`, independent of the `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER` setting.
Number keys 1-9 only choose an option; ⌘↵ carries out the chosen one. Option 1 is pre-selected, so the '1' badge should show only when other options are open.

code.finding: New 'How we got here' flow built from each case's own data (portal, reader, verifier, prediction, approval rule, decision, then); missing steps are omitted rather than invented. Evolved from a two-column snake to a single top-to-bottom column using the routine diagram's connectors, with a Full/Less toggle and 'Open' links to the evidence drawer.

workflow: Subagents are effective for large cross-checks (200 order confirmations and 59 scans in one run) and for drawing design variants without touching the repo.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change; a 'no files modified' skip does not mean the hooks failed.
Visual UI changes were verified with headless-Chrome screenshots at desktop and phone sizes on a copy of demo state, which caught layout and wording problems before merging.
Feature work was kept on separate branches (`jonas/pulse-ui`, `jonas/case-flow`) in sibling worktree folders; a mistaken merge was reverted cleanly because nothing was pushed.
Interview notes and team memory (Entire Brain) were consulted to settle a design direction; user feedback pushed toward decision-first views over chat.

friction: Misread what the team liked about Pulse: built a duplicate chat UI when the flow view was wanted, then had to undo the merge.
The two-column case flow read right-to-left on the second row and was confusing; it needed a rewrite to a single column.
The top bar became crowded, with status running into the menu; it needed a 3-column grid and trimmed labels at narrower widths.
Phone issues: empty-looking collapsed flow, a bottom action bar overlapping options, and the page auto-scrolling to the case list on load.
Several UI pieces were never verified in a real browser (the Describe chat draft, the Details toggle click, the folded view with shorter connectors).
The hand-in time was misunderstood as 12:00 and repeatedly raised, then corrected to 12:45 by the user.
Unclear whether portal data and supplier replies are identical across teams; this needs an answer from the Lio engineers.
Could not reproduce the 'Ask Maren to approve' button jumping the user reported.
The Docs MCP, artifacts and the portal login pasted in Discord created extra handling overhead; the password may need rotating.
open_items: Push `main` (about 19+ commits ahead of origin) before the 12:45 hand-in and restart live so it serves the new server code.
The `jonas/pulse-ui` branch with the 'Describe it' chat remains parked and unmerged.

Support 'send the email, then chase once if no answer' on decision routines, which needs a follow-up watcher on the reply.
Choose and apply a Lighthouse logo variant (assistant recommends 3, subagent recommends 2) to favicon, top bar and sign-in.
Consider a phone bottom-sheet for 'All cases' after the hand-in.
Register sender addresses in portal Settings and decide on an inbox; send the Karton Nowak art-book order (24 h offer) and answer Boise's EXW/DDP question through the product.
Briefing page and doc still reflect the 14:00 state, not the 14:37 drop and later changes.
